system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager
T5: Over-crediting Backstage plugin development
T6: Old cover letter is to her current employer and says she is at Brightwater

# OUTPUT 1: CV
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including 6 years operating
Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in designing and running cloud environments, building
Terraform-managed infrastructure, and leading platform initiatives from implementation through production.
Focused on reliable, observable platforms and self-service infrastructure that helps product teams deploy and
operate services effectively.
CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Terraform,
Atlantis, Kubernetes, Linux, Puppet
Platform and delivery: Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Crossplane, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error
budgets, incident management
Programming and testing: Go, Python, Bash, k6
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS) Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 –
Present
• Technical lead for a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform of 8 clusters and
approximately 350 services across 3 regions.
• Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service
provisioning for RDS, SQS, and S3; reduced the time to take a new service to production from approximately 2
weeks to under 1 day.
• Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing on-call pages per week by
approximately 60%.
• Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
• Serve in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
• Operated AWS game backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS, and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million
daily active players.
• Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules and used Atlantis for
pull-request-based plan and apply workflows.
• Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, and Loki observability stack.
• Conducted pre-launch load testing with k6 and supported launch-day capacity planning.
Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
• Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
• Automated infrastructure tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.
EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016
CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023
LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to apply for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity
role at Corvale Mobility. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years
operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a track record of taking platform initiatives from
design and implementation through to production. Corvale’s need to shape a reliable,
observable and secure foundation for connecting its new train fleet with cloud services is a
strong match for my infrastructure and platform background.
In my current role as Senior Platform Engineer at Tallybrook, I lead a five-person platform
team operating eight AWS EKS clusters across three regions, supporting approximately 350
services. I built an internal developer platform using service templates, Argo CD and
Crossplane self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3, reducing the time to take a new
service to production from around two weeks to under one day. I also introduced SLOs and
error budgets for critical services, reducing weekly on-call pages by approximately 60%, and
moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
My earlier experience includes running AWS game-backend infrastructure for titles with up to
1.2 million daily active players, managing infrastructure through Terraform and Atlantis, and
operating Linux environments at scale. Across these roles, I have led technical work, supported
service teams, and established practices that help systems remain operable in production. I
would bring that experience to Corvale’s infrastructure design, Terraform repository, and service
deployment support, while helping product teams operate services reliably in production.
Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on end-to-end ownership resonate with the
way I work: building dependable platforms that help teams deliver and operate services
effectively. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform
and platform engineering experience could support the Fleet Connectivity team.
Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
